input.quote: (b) Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: The audit right binding us (Article II, Record Keeping and Reports (b)) contains no frequency cap, so Licensor may demand audits without limit — walk-away territory under the rule — and it gives no minimum notice period (we must merely permit the audit within 30 days of a demand), failing the fallback's "once per year on 15 days' notice". Cost allocation at p0064 is already at the preferred position (Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy exceeds 5%) and the clause is limited to accounting records with no system-access right, so we left those untouched. Redline adds the frequency cap, 30 days' prior notice, business-hours limitation, auditor confidentiality and an express no-system-access statement; one audit per year on 15 days' notice is our stated fallback.

ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
ops.newText: Any such audit shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice from Licensor, during Licensee's normal business hours and in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Licensee's operations, and the auditor shall be bound by written obligations of confidentiality to Licensee. Licensor shall have no direct access to Licensee's systems, networks or data.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We limited the records audit to once in any twelve-month period on thirty days' prior written notice, during business hours and by an auditor bound by confidentiality, with no direct access to our systems; as drafted the audit right is unlimited in frequency and can be demanded without meaningful notice. We can accept one audit per year on fifteen days' notice if that is easier.
proposal.summary: Cap audit frequency at once per 12 months, require 30 days' notice, business hours, confidentiality-bound auditor and no system access.
